- Family and target: hook h1b, the dollar total for the one FY 2024 category whose fee no document prints (GSO), reached through the 60/40 allocation from an NGSO share rebuilt out of D05's units and D06's per-unit fees. Target medium (user, 2026-10-13: no Easy slot, "target medium and high"). Quick test survived (user chat 2026-10-13); no Checks run or difficulty run yet.
- What the quick tests on this hook showed (user chat 2026-10-13, verbatim: "1, 3 too easy, 2 survived. others not tested"; no panels): the two share forms, q01 (NGSO-Other, 31.5%) and i03 (per-system payors, 39.4%), were answered by the easier solver, and both need the small-satellite placement and the total through the 40% share. So the easier solver clears those two steps. This question needs the same steps and survived; the one difference is that nothing about the asked category is priced in the documents (the share forms have a printed numerator). The easier solver's answer here is unknown: route unread. The survival is one preliminary screen beside two failed siblings, not a measured difficulty.
- Dependency plan: (1) D05 para 28: FY 2024 units 11, 6, 16 (and 140 GSO units, not needed for the total). (2) D06 para 40: per-unit fees $964,200 and $441,925, and the clause putting small-satellite fees inside the NGSO share. (3) D06 para 7: $12,215. (4) NGSO share 10,606,200 + 2,651,550 + 195,440 = 13,453,190. (5) D05 paras 9 and 34: 60% GSO / 40% NGSO for FY 2024. (6) 13,453,190 / 40 x 60 = 20,179,785 -> $20.2 million.
- Unpointed steps (audit before the first run): the question names the year, the category, "as a group" and the precision. Not pointed at: (a) no GSO fee is printed, so the figure must come from the other side of the 60/40 allocation (D05 paras 9, 34); (b) small-satellite fees sit inside the NGSO share (D06 para 40); (c) 60/40, not the earlier 80/20, for FY 2024 (D05 para 34). Steps (b) and the scaling were cleared by the easier solver on the sibling wordings, so they are not expected to hold it; what held it here is not yet known.
- Universe: the four FY 2024 space station fee categories (D05 para 3). GSO is the asked one; the other three make up the NGSO share.
- Necessity: D05 -> the unit counts 11, 6 and 16 (only source; "units" searched in D02, D06, D07) and the statement that 60/40 was the case for FY 2024. Without D05 the NGSO share cannot be valued. D06 -> the two per-unit fees (only source; no other document prints $964,200 or $441,925). Without D06 nothing is priced except the small-satellite fee. D02 also states the deduction rule; D06 para 40 states it, so D02 is neither ticked nor cited.
- Selected-lever checks: scatter: units in D05, fees in D06, allocation in D05. Rounding: 20,179,785 rounds to $20.2 million; per-unit fees are rounded to the nearest $5, which moves the result between 20,179,721 and 20,179,849, the same $20.2 million. Not a which-items question; no rounded-prose lever claimed.
- Targeted failure modes: Part vs total -> $19.9 million: (10,606,200 + 2,651,550) / 40 x 60 = 19,886,625 (recomputed 2026-10-13); the same figure results from adding small-satellite fees outside the split. Considered and not declared: the earlier 80% GSO / 20% NGSO allocation ($53.8 million: 13,453,190 / 20 x 80 = 53,812,760). Neither has been observed; the sibling quick tests suggest the easier solver does not make the first slip. Re-align the mode with the run's actual wrong answers before Submit.
- Calculation verification: script with exact fractions, 2026-10-13: 13,453,190 / 40 = 336,329.75; x 60 = 20,179,785. Units: U.S. dollars, answer in millions to one decimal. Cross-check of the rule: 10,606,200 : 2,651,550 = exactly 4 : 1. Cross-check outside the bundle (not evidence, not cited; web search 2026-10-13): 47 CFR 1.1156 as reproduced online lists $144,155 for GSO stations beside the $12,215 small-satellite fee (fiscal year of the row not stated in the results); 140 x 144,155 = 20,181,700, also $20.2 million.

The overview lists the splits and $12,215 only. Shortest complete route: D05 para 28, D05 para 9 or 34, D06 paras 7 and 40. No passage states the answer.

(1) "Cannot be determined, no GSO fee is printed": the 60% GSO / 40% NGSO allocation of space station regulatory fees is stated outright for FY 2024, so the figure follows; whether the form's solvers accept a derived figure will show in "One defensible answer". (4) Per-station fee instead of the group total: "as a group" rejects it.

sections.question: To the nearest $0.1 million, how much in regulatory fees did the FCC assess on geostationary space stations as a group for fiscal year 2024?
sections.reasoning:
Step 1. Source input (Doc 5, its paragraph on how few units pay space station fees): for FY 2024 there were 11 units of other NGSO space stations, 6 units of less complex NGSO space stations and 16 units of small satellite fee payors. The same sentence counts the GSO space stations but no document prints the fee each of them paid.

Step 2. Source input (Doc 6, its paragraph on the current NGSO fee split): for fiscal year 2024 each NGSO-Other payor was assessed $964,200 and each NGSO-Less Complex payor $441,925. The same paragraph says that 80% and 20% of the NGSO share go to these categories after a pro rata amount of the small satellite fees is subtracted from each, so the small satellite fees are paid out of the NGSO share.

Step 3. Source input (Doc 6, its background paragraph on the June 2024 order): the small satellite fee for FY 2024 was $12,215 per license.

Step 4. Calculation (Doc 5 and Doc 6): NGSO-Other fees, in dollars: 11 × 964,200 = 10,606,200

Step 5. Calculation (Doc 5 and Doc 6): NGSO-Less Complex fees, in dollars: 6 × 441,925 = 2,651,550

Step 6. Calculation (Doc 5 and Doc 6): small satellite fees, in dollars: 16 × 12,215 = 195,440

Step 7. Calculation (Doc 5 and Doc 6): the NGSO share is the sum of these fees, in dollars: 10,606,200 + 2,651,550 + 195,440 = 13,453,190

Step 8. Source input (Doc 5, its background paragraph on September 2024 and its later remark on FY 2024): for FY 2024 the Commission allocated 60% of space station regulatory fees to GSO payors and 40% to NGSO payors, so the GSO stations' fees follow from the NGSO share.

Step 9. Calculation (Doc 5 and Doc 6): each percentage point of all space station regulatory fees, in dollars: 13,453,190 / 40 = 336,329.75

Step 10. Calculation (Doc 5 and Doc 6): the GSO stations' fees as a group, in dollars: 336,329.75 × 60 = 20,179,785

Step 11. Final answer (Doc 5 and Doc 6): rounded to the nearest tenth of a million dollars, as the question asks, 20,179,785 dollars is twenty point two million dollars.
sections.targeted failure modes:
### Failure mode 1
Trap: Part vs total
How a careless solver fails: Takes the wrong line item

Why these are traps: Part vs total: Doc 6 prices only NGSO-Other and Less Complex, but the 40% NGSO share (Doc 5) also holds small satellite fees. Scaling those two categories alone by 60/40 gives $19.9 million. Adding Doc 5's 16 small satellite units at $12,215 first gives $20.2 million.
